meta.title: CAPLE A2 — Portuguese
meta.subtitle: 500 words · European Portuguese · both directions
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck, as two cards per word: Portuguese → English (see the Portuguese, recall the meaning) and English → Portuguese (see an English meaning, recall the Portuguese). 500 words for level A2 of the Common European Framework, which is the level of CIPLE, the exam awarded by CAPLE — the Centro de Avaliação de Português Língua Estrangeira at the Universidade de Lisboa. None of them appears in the A1 deck, so the two together come to 1,000 words. THIS DECK TEACHES EUROPEAN PORTUGUESE. CAPLE sets its exams on the European standard, so the train is o comboio and the bus o autocarro; the mood is the conjuntivo and not the subjuntivo; and the first person plural of the preterite is falámos, not falamos. That choice reaches into every part of the deck rather than sitting in this description: the frequency ordering is taken from the European half of the subtitle corpus and not the Brazilian one, Wiktionary's Brazil-marked verb forms and word senses are excluded, and example sentences carrying a Brazilian marker are rejected. Where the reference inventory gives both a European and a Brazilian word for the same thing — it writes them together, as uma chávena/xícara de — the deck teaches the European one. There is no published CAPLE word list — the exam board publishes exam specifications and no vocabulary inventory — so the words are taken from the reference description CAPLE's own resources page points at: the Referencial Camões PLE, the Instituto Camões' level-by-level account of Portuguese, whose A2 inventory of Noções is read for the topical vocabulary and whose Funções and Gramática sections supply the greetings, the courtesy formulas and the closed classes that a list of notions names without ever writing out. Only the inventory of words is taken; none of the Referencial's own prose appears in this deck. The cards are ordered roughly by how common the word is in everyday European Portuguese, so the words you will meet most often come first: the order comes from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, with a reflexive verb placed by the verb it is formed from. Every noun carries its article, so the gender is learnt with the word (231 of them), and its plural sits directly beneath it; the article is coloured for its gender. A noun or adjective with a distinct feminine is taught as a pair rather than as two words (57 of them): o professor, a professora above os professores, as professoras. Each of the 154 verbs carries its full conjugation — the non-finite forms, all six simple tenses of the indicative, the three of the conjuntivo, both imperatives, and the personal infinitive, which is the one tense Portuguese has that no other Romance language does. Six persons are shown, from eu to eles; você and vocês are named on the third-person rows, which is where they take their verb and the single most confusing thing about the Portuguese verb for a beginner. The 20 reflexive verbs are conjugated the European way, with the pronoun after the verb rather than in front of it, including the first person plural that drops its -s before -nos and the future and conditional, where the pronoun goes inside the verb. The pronoun is picked out in colour so its three positions can be seen at a glance; in ordinary writing it is joined to the verb with hyphens, as chamo-me, levanta-te, chamamo-nos and chamar-me-ei. Real example sentences come with 492 of the 500 words, three apiece for 488 of them and one or two for the rest; the sentence corpus has nothing at all for the remaining 8, which are kept because the word list is set by the reference inventory and not by the corpus, chosen where possible to show three different inflected forms rather than the same one three times, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside it. Tatoeba's Portuguese is overwhelmingly Brazilian, so sentences carrying a Brazilian marker are rejected outright; what remains is mostly variety-neutral rather than positively European, which is a limit of the corpus and not something the filter can repair. Word list: Referencial Camões PLE (instituto-camoes.pt). Meanings, genders, plurals and conjugations: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency ordering: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

cards.question: já
cards.answer: already (indicating that something has happened before); now (at this instant)
cards.answerText: already (indicating that something has happened before); now (at this instant)

fields.English:
adverb
  • already (indicating that something has happened before)
  • now (at this instant)
fields.Examples:
Você já fez o seu dever de casa?
Did you already do your homework?
Na verdade, eu já vi este filme antes.
Actually, I've seen this movie before.
Você já voltou para casa antes das sete?
Have you ever returned home before seven?

fields.English:
adjective
  • only
  • just (alone in a category)
fields.Examples:
Só posso dizer-te o que sei.
I can only tell you what I know.
Gostaria de falar com você a sós.
I'd like to talk with you in private.
A aula só começa às oito e meia.
Class doesn't begin until eight-thirty.

fields.English:
pronoun
  • everything (all the things)
  • everyone
  • all
fields.Examples:
Parece-me que ela sabe de tudo.
It seems to me that she knows everything.
Dê-me tempo para lhe dar tudo o que eu tenho!
Give me time to give you everything I have!
Conte-me tudo sobre a viagem que você fez.
Tell me all about the trip you've made.

cards.question: lá
cards.answer: there; used with an adverb phrase to indicate that something is far
cards.answerText: there; used with an adverb phrase to indicate that something is far

fields.English:
adverb

Sabe-se lá de onde veio isso.

Pode-se ir até lá de carro?

fields.English:
pronoun
nothing (not any thing; no thing)

Os homens não sabem nada sobre as mulheres.

fields.English:
adjective

Somos da mesma idade, mas de alturas diferentes.

Numa democracia, os cidadãos têm os mesmos direitos.

fields.English:
adjective
  • full of
  • replete
fields.Examples:

Pode-se dizer assim, mas é muito vulgar.

Parece-me que as coisas seriam melhor assim.

cards.question: ainda
cards.answer: still; yet (up to a time); even (emphasises a comparative)
cards.answerText: still; yet (up to a time); even (emphasises a comparative)

fields.English:
adverb

  • even (emphasises a comparative)

adverb

cards.answer: not even (introduces an emphatic negation); do not even (introduces an emphatic negative command)

fields.English:
